# `aitbc wallet create`

Create a new wallet with an optional type and password encryption. The encryption password resolves through the WAL-1 standard sources: ``--password-stdin``/``--password-file``/``--password`` (deprecated), ``AITBC_WALLET_PASSWORD_FILE``, ``AITBC_WALLET_PASSWORD[_<NAME>]``, the system keyring, or — on a TTY only — the two-prompt confirm loop, which also stores it in the keyring. ``--no-encrypt`` skips resolution entirely and cannot be combined with a password flag.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc wallet create [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--name` | text | — | yes | Wallet name. |
| `--type` | text | `hd` | no | Wallet type (hd, simple) |
| `--no-encrypt` | flag | `false` | no | Skip wallet encryption (not recommended) |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc wallet create --name <name>
```
